clue.text: Ops (for Greece) appended to journal otherwise showing verbal incontinence

indicators.note: something appended is tacked on at the end, so this piece follows the others

parts.note: a log is a daily record or journal
or, as in 'or else'
Ops was the Roman mother goddess; her Greek counterpart is Rhea

explanation.surface: A rambling piece about a Greek goddess tacked onto a diary entry suggests a writer who cannot stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Ops is the Roman name; '(for Greece)' asks for her Greek equivalent, Rhea.
explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is excessive, uncontrolled talkativeness, a flood of words likened to a medical complaint.

clue.text: Old coot, 52, smoker, to entertain Romeo

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so this letter goes inside the others

parts.note: LII is 52 in Roman numerals
a pipe is something one smokes

explanation.surface: An elderly codger, aged 52 and fond of a pipe, plays host to a Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is R in the phonetic alphabet; it sits after the first two letters of the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a hood's long tail, Chambers gives liripipe (or liripoop) as an obsolete word for a silly fellow, a fool.

clue.text: Stop insulting ambassador's hosts

indicators.note: the words play host to the answer, holding it within their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A plea to end rudeness towards an ambassador's dinner hosts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like a command but is the organ-stop sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamba is an organ stop with a string-like tone, named after the viola da gamba.

clue.text: I DJ and I am in pub getting over arthritis treatment

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the other word
in a down entry, getting over means turning upwards, so this word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a bar is a pub
the letter I taken as written
a DJ is a dinner jacket, which Americans call a tux
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: A disc jockey's boast about being in the pub while getting over arthritis.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ is not the disc jockey but a dinner jacket, a tux.
explanation.definitionFit: Rituximab is a monoclonal antibody drug used for rheumatoid arthritis as well as some cancers.

clue.text: Caught giving way to large, carefree lout

indicators.note: one letter yields its place to another, a swap

parts.note: halcyon days are calm, untroubled ones

explanation.surface: Someone caught yielding to a large, happy-go-lucky yob.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught, and it is swapped for L in the word for carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallyon (also hallion) is a Scots and dialect word for a worthless, rough fellow, a lout.

clue.text: Arizona, then some old Northern Isles, leaving North Dakota to climb height in Italy

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means reading from the bottom up
these letters depart from the place name, which loses them

parts.note: Zetland is the old name for Shetland, an island group north of Scotland

explanation.surface: A travelogue roaming from Arizona to the Shetlands and North Dakota before climbing an Italian peak.
explanation.walkthrough: AZ and ND are US state abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Altezza is the Italian word for height, and also for highness as a title.

clue.text: Almost tight-lipped about fruit available in winter

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are read in reverse
almost the whole word, so it loses its final letter

parts.note: saying nothing, silent

explanation.surface: Someone saying very little about the fruit on offer during winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelis is a variety of pear, the winter nelis, which keeps well and ripens in the cold months.

clue.text: Pre-flight brief in the afternoon only?

wordplay.note: read as 'not a.m.', i.e. never in the morning

explanation.surface: A query whether a pilot's briefing is held only after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the phrase is split as NOT AM, the morning being a.m.
explanation.definitionFit: A NOTAM, short for 'notice to airmen', is the official bulletin pilots read before flying.

clue.text: Set up leader for military routines to support line with wartime levy

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits beneath the others

parts.note: and, as in 'bread and butter'

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means raised, so the letters read upwards
the leader is the first letter of the word

parts.note: its leader is its opening letter
ruts are dull fixed routines

explanation.surface: Raising a commander for drill to back up the front line in a wartime draft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Landsturm was the German and Swiss reserve militia called up in wartime, a general levy of the population.

clue.text: The Bard's lofty play's ending with runner around, not a word

indicators.note: the runner wraps around this letter

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word whose last letter is wanted
sh! is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean drama's lofty finale, with an athlete running round in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare, who used this word in Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Skyish, Shakespeare's coinage, means sky-high, reaching towards the heavens.

clue.text: Single plant removing jack from aircraft engine

indicators.note: this letter is taken out of the engine

parts.note: a ramjet is a simple jet engine with no compressor

explanation.surface: A lone factory site stripping a jack out of a jet engine.
explanation.walkthrough: J is jack in card notation. 'Plant' looks industrial but is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a ramet is one individual member of a clone, a single plant grown from the same stock.

clue.text: Lurking giant with frilly clothing

indicators.note: one word clothes the other, wrapping round it

parts.note: lacy, trimmed with frills
a titan is a giant

explanation.surface: A giant hiding about in ruffled clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitancy is the state of lying hidden or concealed, a rare noun for skulking.

clue.text: Expelling English, following through to perform ceilidh music

indicators.note: this piece runs through the middle of the other

parts.note: to play is to perform

indicators.note: this letter is thrown out of the word

parts.note: next, as in coming after

explanation.surface: After the English are sent off, the band carries on playing at a Celtic dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A planxty is an Irish harp tune, typically composed in honour of a patron, played at such gatherings.

clue.text: Back half of slimy northern bog in which one goes fermenting

indicators.note: only the latter half of the word is kept

parts.note: oozy, wet and slimy

indicators.note: the bog is where this letter ends up
the letter goes into the bog

parts.note: in Scotland and northern England a moss is a peat bog

explanation.surface: Something rotting in the slimy rear part of a northern marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Zymosis is fermentation, the process by which yeasts and enzymes break down substances.

clue.text: Phlox-related tree planted among prepared taro by company boss in Australia

indicators.note: a tree planted among something stands inside it

parts.note: poi is the Hawaiian paste of cooked, pounded taro root
a lemon is a citrus tree

indicators.note: the boss is placed inside the country's code

parts.note: AUS is the international code for Australia
chief executive officer

explanation.surface: A gardening note on a phlox relative growing among taro beside a corporate chief down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox belongs to the Polemoniaceae, the Jacob's ladder family, so polemoniaceous plants are its botanical kin.

clue.text: Noble cause scuppered when knight leaves compound for change of colours

indicators.note: a scuppered plan is wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the knight departs, so his letter is removed

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the raw material
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A noble enterprise is wrecked when its knight rides away.
explanation.definitionFit: A leuco base is a colourless reduced form of a dye that turns coloured on oxidation, used in dyeing.

clue.text: Snake poison drug criticised before the watershed?

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come ahead of this one

parts.note: E is ecstasy
chid is an old past tense of chide
British TV's watershed falls at 9 p.m., after which adult content may air

explanation.surface: A broadcasting row: a programme about a drug slammed for airing too early in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Echidnine is an old name for the venomous principle in viper venom, from Greek echidna, a viper.

clue.text: Murdered 26 offspring when duty includes reversing former denial

parts.note: as, as in 'as it happened'

indicators.note: the duty contains the other piece

parts.note: a tax is a duty

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: nay is an old-fashioned no

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a child killed when taxes involved going back on an old refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is ILIAN, Trojan; the Trojan child here is Hector's son, hurled from the walls of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Astyanax, son of Hector and Andromache, was killed by the Greeks after Troy fell.

clue.text: Discovered Marseillaise and moods in Morningside mashup?

parts.note: rumbled means found out
et is French for and, as in France's anthem
a hump is a fit of sulks

explanation.surface: Revolutionary song and sulks found in a mash-up of genres.
explanation.walkthrough: Morningside is a genteel district of Edinburgh, pointing to a Scottish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbledethumps is a Borders dish of potato, cabbage and onion mashed together, often baked with cheese.

clue.text: Pack down under being in print?

indicators.note: in a down entry this piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: en is French for in
to stamp is to tread something down firm

explanation.surface: Packing down below while a book goes to press.
explanation.definitionFit: To enstamp is to impress a mark or design on something, an old verb for imprinting.

clue.text: The woman mostly seen in Somerset hills, out of bounds for ancient village

indicators.note: this piece is placed within the other
the word loses its bounding letters at both ends

parts.note: the Mendips are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, England

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: she

explanation.surface: A woman spotted in the Somerset hills, straying beyond the limits of an old village.
explanation.definitionFit: Endship is an archaic English word for a small settlement or hamlet.

clue.text: Love feasts? Answer is opening wide!

definitions.note: the plural noun matches the plural answer

parts.note: gapes, as a mouth does

explanation.surface: A diner opens wide at a lavish banquet of love.
explanation.definitionFit: Agapes were the communal meals of the early Christians, named from the Greek word for brotherly love.

clue.text: American architect builds, having scored more for width

indicators.note: one piece stands in for the other

parts.note: grows, as in builds up
più is the Italian musical direction for more, written on scores

explanation.surface: An architect enlarging projects after outscoring rivals on width.
explanation.walkthrough: W for width; più appears in scores such as 'più forte'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Gropius, founder of the Bauhaus, emigrated to the United States and taught at Harvard.

clue.text: Selecting odd bits from 7, I should replace the first, to put it briefly

indicators.note: a new letter takes over the opening position
taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on

parts.note: the answer to clue 7, the wartime levy
the letter I taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor picks scraps from another item and asserts editorial control, in short.
explanation.walkthrough: The 7 refers to the entry in this puzzle; its odd letters are then altered at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag 'in sum' means in summary, in a few words.

clue.text: Traveller made a tour of island before retiring

indicators.note: the first pieces come ahead of this one

parts.note: did, as in 'we did Rome in a day'
coy, shy and modest

explanation.surface: A tourist visits an island before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like going to bed but means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: A didicoy is an itinerant person, a member of the Irish or Romany travelling community.

clue.text: Scale, one with no sharp or flat extension

parts.words: one with no sharp or flat
parts.note: the scale of C major has no sharps or flats
a limb extends from the body

explanation.surface: A musical scale without accidentals, plus an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks musical, and the next words continue that, but the definition is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or cliff is to climb it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Commendation for everyone sharing first helping of Eton mess

parts.note: praise

indicators.note: the two words share this letter, so it appears only once

parts.note: each, as in 'a pound each'

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: the school's first letter is the shared one

clue.text: Catch one that's retrograde like Ganymede

indicators.note: moving backwards, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: to nail someone is to catch them

explanation.surface: An astronomer catches a moon in backward orbit, like Jupiter's Ganymede.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede is a moon of Jupiter, but here the Trojan prince carried off by Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilian means Trojan, of Ilium, and Ganymede was a prince of Troy.

clue.text: East London rascal shook hollow tree

elm

explanation.walkthrough: East London is a city in South Africa, not the East End; the word is South African and Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: A skelm is a scoundrel or rogue in South African English, from Dutch schelm.

clue.text: Hothead to be just visible across very soft hedge bush
